heard: One star is sprinting across our night sky faster than any other. Barnard's star travels the apparent width of the full moon roughly every 180 years. Located roughly six light years away, it is our closest neighbor after the Alpha Centauri system. Yet despite its proximity, this red dwarf is too dim to see with the unaided eye. It is blue-shifted and racing straight toward our sun at roughly 110 kilometers per second. For over half a century, astronomers announced giant planets around it, only to debunk them as telescope errors. Astronomers finally confirmed genuine exoplanets orbiting the star in 2024 and 2025. Those worlds are locked into a cosmic journey that leaves every other star behind.
